newsitem.title: USA: California park closed after water slide disaster.
newsitem.headline: California park closed after water slide disaster.

text.p: A popular California amusement park will remain closed while investigators try to determine what caused a water slide to collapse, killing one teen-ager and injuring 32 others, officials said Tuesday.

Many of the teens were seriously hurt -- some with life-threatening injuries -- when part of the 40-foot (12-metre)-tall winding slide collapsed on Monday at Waterworld USA, owned by Premier Parks Inc.
Premier Parks said Waterworld in Concord, California, about 30 miles (50 km) northeast of San Francisco, would remain closed and no date had been set to re-open it.
"The park will remain closed until we and the city agree that it is appropriate to re-open," said Jim Dannhauser, chief financial officer for Premier Parks.

Teen-agers on the water slide, called the Banzai Pipeline, plummeted to the ground when it collapsed, turning the pool of water below red with blood. Many of the injured broke bones in the fall and were unconscious when the ambulances arrived.

Waterworld officials said they believed the water slide gave way because a large group of teen-agers had gathered at the top. They were told not to slide down together but ignored the warning, park officials said.
Premier Parks defended its safety record. "Safety is our number-one priority. Based upon what we know at this point, we believe this slide was safe," the company said in a statement.
The city of Concord and local police said they were conducting investigations. Concord said it would hire an independent firm to advise the city.
The injured students were from Napa High School in Napa, California. They were at the park to celebrate their upcoming graduation, school officials said.
"The mood here is very sad, one of disbelief and shock," Napa Valley Unified School District administrative assistant Carolyn Walker said.
The American flag in front of Napa High was flown at half-mast in memory of the student who died.
